title: Console API: expose rollout SLO verdict + rollback history (with pagination + authz)
creator: Chloe Martin
body:
## Context
Console needs to show (a) the current SLO health verdict used by rollout-controller and (b) a timeline of SLO breach events and rollback actions taken (including auto + manual). This ticket adds/extends Console Backend APIs so the UI can render the new “Auto-rollback” panel and “Rollback history” table.

This is explicitly *read* APIs for Console; write actions (pause policy / manual ack / manual rollback) are handled in separate tickets.

Related docs:
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/auto-rollback-slo-integration-prd
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/auto-rollback-slo-integration-design-spec
- ADR-0147 Monitor identity contract
- ADR-0148 Auto-rollback policy semantics

## Goals
- Provide a single, stable API contract for Console to fetch:
  1) Current verdict state (OK / BREACH / COOLDOWN / WARMUP / UNKNOWN) and the “why” (signal + thresholds + comparison to baseline).
  2) Timeline/history for: breaches detected, rollback triggers, executor actions, and manual overrides.
  3) The effective rollback policy applied for the rollout (including resolved defaults).
- Support pagination for history (cursor-based), time range filtering, and consistent ordering.
- Enforce tenant and role-based access control (customer org membership + environment permissions).

## Non-goals
- UI implementation (handled by Console web).
- Replacing audit logs. We will *reference* audit event IDs and provide a UI-friendly timeline, but audit export remains the system of record.
- Real-time streaming updates (polling is sufficient for v1).

## API surface (proposed)
All endpoints under Console Backend service.

### 1) Get current verdict
GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/slo-verdict

Response (high-level; JSON shape owned by Console Backend):
- rollout_id
- verdict: OK | BREACH | COOLDOWN | WARMUP | UNKNOWN
- evaluated_at (RFC3339)
- evaluation_window: e.g. "5m" / "10m" (string)
- primary_signal: "latency_p95" | "error_rate" (string)
- signals: list of evaluated signals, each includes:
  - signal_name
  - value
  - threshold
  - baseline_value (optional)
  - comparison: "absolute" | "worse_than_baseline"
  - breach: true/false
- gating:
  - min_requests_required (string)
  - min_requests_observed (string)
  - warmup_remaining (string)
  - cooldown_remaining (string)
- monitor_ref:
  - monitor_identity (canonical string form per ADR-0147)
  - monitor_url (string; deep link to dashboards)
- decision_trace_id (string; used to correlate with controller logs)
- last_known_good_version (string)
- candidate_version (string)

Notes:
- `UNKNOWN` is returned when monitors are stale/unavailable or evaluation cannot be performed safely (per ADR-0148). UI should show “Unknown” with a link to monitoring status.
- `WARMUP` indicates rollout in warm-up window where breaches are not actionable; still return computed signals for visibility.

### 2) Get rollback history (timeline)
GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/rollback-history?limit=50&cursor=...&from=...&to=...

Response:
- rollout_id
- items: ordered newest->oldest
- next_cursor (empty if no more)

Each item includes:
- occurred_at
- type:
  - "SLO_BREACH_DETECTED"
  - "AUTO_ROLLBACK_TRIGGERED"
  - "ROLLBACK_EXECUTOR_ACTION"
  - "MANUAL_OVERRIDE"
  - "POLICY_CHANGED"
- summary (short string for UI)
- details (string; UI can render in expandable section)
- actor:
  - "system" or user email/name (string)
- related:
  - audit_event_id (string, when available)
  - incident_id (string, optional)
  - runbook_url (string)

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination using opaque cursor derived from (occurred_at, event_id). Stable ordering required.
- Limit bounds: default 50, max 200.

### 3) Get effective policy (for display)
GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/rollback-policy

Response:
- policy_id
- scope: route/model/region/tier (string representation)
- enabled (true/false as string)
- thresholds (string; includes latency + error policy values)
- evaluation:
  - window
  - required_breaches
  - min_requests
  - warmup_window
  - cooldown
  - must_be_worse_than_baseline (true/false as string)
- fail_behavior: fail_open | fail_closed (string)
- updated_at, updated_by

Implementation note: policy service returns a normalized/resolved view (defaults applied) so Console can display exactly what controller evaluates.

## Data sources
- Verdict: read from rollout-controller’s persisted evaluation state (or controller API) + derived fields for UI.
- History: combine:
  - controller decisioning events (breach + trigger + executor actions)
  - audit log events for policy changes and rollback actions

We should prefer a single backend query for timeline items; if we must stitch, do it server-side and return a merged, ordered list.

## AuthZ / tenancy requirements
- Enforce org/tenant isolation: rollout_id must resolve to an environment + org the caller can access.
- Roles:
  - Read access aligns with existing Rollouts page permissions (Console RBAC). If user can view rollout details, they can view verdict + history.
- Service-to-service calls:
  - Use Console Backend’s service identity when calling controller/audit store.
  - Never expose raw internal monitor query strings to end users; expose monitor URL and identity only.

## Observability
- Add API metrics:
  - request_count, latency_ms (p50/p95), error_rate by endpoint
  - result_size_bytes for rollback-history
- Add structured logs with rollout_id, org_id, environment_id, request_id.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Cursor encoding/decoding and stable pagination ordering
  - AuthZ checks for cross-tenant rollout_id
  - Unknown verdict mapping when upstream returns stale/unavailable
- Integration tests:
  - Seed timeline events and verify merge ordering + cursor
  - Verify returned policy matches resolved defaults from schema service

## Acceptance criteria
- Console can render:
  - Verdict card with verdict state + evaluated_at + primary signal + threshold summary.
  - Rollback history table with pagination and a stable “load more.”
  - Policy display panel with resolved defaults.
- History endpoint supports:
  - limit + cursor
  - from/to time filtering
  - deterministic ordering (no duplicates/missing items across pages)
- AuthZ:
  - Attempt to access a rollout from another org/environment returns 404 (preferred) or 403 per existing Console patterns.
- Error handling:
  - If controller/audit store is unavailable, verdict returns UNKNOWN with reason in `details` and history returns partial data only if explicitly safe; otherwise 503.

## Implementation plan
1) Define proto/contract in console-backend and align with Console web (Dylan Brooks / Design).
2) Implement verdict endpoint backed by rollout-controller evaluation state.
3) Implement timeline endpoint backed by audit store + controller events; merge server-side.
4) Implement effective policy endpoint backed by policy service (schema resolver).
5) Add metrics/logging and update API docs.

## Open questions
- Do we need environment scoping in path (e.g., /environments/{env_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/...)? For now, rollout_id lookup includes env/org and we keep existing Console patterns.
- Should history include raw SLO values at time of breach? For v1, keep `details` human-readable; we can add typed fields later without breaking UI.
comments: 2025-02-03 (Felix Schneider): Drafted API shapes and shared with Console web. Request from Dylan: include `decision_trace_id` so UI can deep link to controller logs/traces.

2025-02-05 (Jada Williams): For verdict endpoint, please map controller states 1:1. In particular, we need explicit `UNKNOWN` when monitor is stale (see hotfix work in controller). Don’t collapse into OK.

2025-02-07 (Sean Gallagher): History needs to surface whether rollback was auto vs manual, and include the audit_event_id so oncall can correlate quickly. +1 to returning 404 for unauthorized to avoid leaking rollout existence.
2025-02-11 (Felix Schneider): Implemented cursor-based pagination (occurred_at + event_id). Added max limit=200. Added integration test for no-dup across pages when events share the same timestamp.

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Please ensure we don’t return monitor query strings. OK to return monitor identity + dashboard URL. Also make sure org_id/env_id are in structured logs for support debugging.

2025-02-18 (Felix Schneider): Hooked history items to audit log where available; for controller-only events (breach detected), generating UI summary + details server-side. Added `runbook_url` to each item type with default runbook link.
2025-02-21 (Felix Schneider): Merged in PR-18503. Console web unblocked; QA to verify with staged rollout cohort.
